## Intent
Hypothesis: expressing the per-particle update as a branchless blend with hash RNG in Halide enables parallel auto-scheduling that approaches the streaming bandwidth ceiling.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is FLAT across all N. At q=0.01, single-thread cost holds at 60.4 ns/p (N=10000, past L2 spill at N≈7710) and falls slightly to 56.4 ns/p at N=10M (past L3 spill at N≈246723) — no knee at either spill. Death rate raises the floor uniformly: at N=10M, 56.4 ns/p (q=0.01) to 66.8 ns/p (q=0.5), without reshaping the curve. Multi-threaded rows (~440 ns/p) are likewise flat across N.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 1.2 GB/s at N=10M, q=0.01 — 9.5% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound: no cache-spill knee appears, and multi-threading collapses throughput to 0.15 GB/s (440 ns/p). Frontend_stall dominates at 53.4% (threads=1, N=10M) rising to 89–90% (threads=4/8), with backend_stall at 0% single-threaded. No regime approaches the ceiling.

## Assembly
No vectorization. The histogram reports zero packed vector instructions; all FP ops are scalar — vmulss, vaddss, vsubss, vucomiss, vcvttss2si. Loads are vmovss from [rcx-0x8], [rcx-0x4], [rcx] with rcx advancing 0x44 (68 bytes) per particle — no gather, no packed load. The render loop does byte-granular scatter stores: mov BYTE PTR [r13+r15*1+0x0] with saturating add via cmp bx,0xff / cmovae. The 413-instruction body (147 mov, 42 lea) with scalar-only execution explains the 53% frontend stall.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 1.2 GB/s (9.5% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling). Zero packed vector instructions were emitted (all scalar vmulss/vaddss), and parallel scheduling makes performance 7× worse (440 vs 56 ns/p). Frontend stalls at 53–90% confirm the bottleneck is scalar instruction delivery, not memory bandwidth.
